data.title: Blackstone's Top Private-Equity Executive Is Preparing to Leave Firm — WSJ
data.description:
By Miriam Gottfried and AnnaMaria Andriotis

Blackstone's top private-equity executive, Joseph Baratta, is preparing to leave the firm, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest in a series of departures by senior leaders from the private-investment giant.

Baratta, who has been with Blackstone for nearly three decades, has been the firm's global head of private equity since 2012 and is one of its most senior executives. He is also a Blackstone board member and part of the firm's management committee. The exact timing of his departure hasn't been determined, but it is likely to come around the end of this year, the people said.

A spokeswoman for Blackstone confirmed Baratta's pending departure.

Senior executives at Blackstone have long faced the reality that Jonathan Gray, the firm's 56-year-old president, is expected to succeed CEO Stephen Schwarzman. Schwarzman, 79 years old, co-founded Blackstone in 1985. That leaves few paths for growth for someone as senior as Baratta, 55. Earlier this month, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nadeem Meghji, Blackstone's global head of real estate, was leaving the firm.

Write to Miriam Gottfried at Miriam.Gottfried@wsj.com and AnnaMaria Andriotis at annamaria.andriotis@wsj.com

data.title: How Nvidia Can Benefit From Musk's SpaceX Chip Surprise — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Clark

Nvidia can always count on Elon Musk. The billionaire businessman has just laid out how many artificial-intelligence chips he expects to buy for his SpaceX company's xAI business.

Musk said overnight that the xAI's Memphis data-center complex, called "Colossus," already houses around 780,000 Nvidia AI chips, split across its Hopper and Blackwell generations. The company expects another 220,000 of Nvidia's GB300 Blackwell chips to be operational next week, followed by another 220,000 in October.

"If we get lucky, yet another 220k GB300 by late December," Musk posted on social-media platform X.

Colossus was always set to incorporate a minimum of one million graphics-processing units, according to a statement from the city's chamber of commerce, and Musk previously said SpaceX would exclusively use Nvidia AI chips.

But the latest figures indicate Colossus could house as many as 1.44 million chips before the end of the year, spread across the Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 facilities. The pace of expansion is impressive. And it could help soothe concerns about whether technology companies are overpromising about their abilities to construct data-centers quickly.

For example, Oracle has run into issues with its "Project Jupiter" data-center campus in New Mexico, leading it to deliver a contractual notice to potentially delay payments to its developer, according to The Wall Street Journal. Oracle said in a statement that the project remains on schedule.

Nvidia needs data-center construction to keep pace with its chip sales in order to avoid a glut of hardware sitting in inventories. Musk is doing his part.

Nvidia shares rose 0.1% to $224.86 on Friday.

"Nvidia, of course, is at the epicenter of AI, with an 80% growth rate, and you're paying 22 times forward earnings," said Ken Mahoney, CEO of Mahoney Asset Management. "Typically, Nvidia trades between, let's say, 20 to 40 times forward earnings...It looks actually cheap here."

Write to Adam Clark at adam.clark@barrons.com

data.title: Mounting rate hike bets keep weekly loss in sight for gold
data.description:
Key points:
  • Spot gold down about 2.1% so far in the week
  • Oil prices drop about 3%
  • Silver, platinum, palladium also set for weekly declines

By Anjana Anil

Gold prices edged higher on Friday but were headed for a weekly loss, as concerns about sticky inflation, hawkish signals from Federal Reserve policymakers, and higher US Treasury yields dented bullion's appeal.

Spot gold was up 0.1% at $4,282.98 per ounce by 2:05 p.m. ET (1805 GMT). Prices were headed for a weekly loss, down about 2.1% so far. US gold futures settled 0.5% higher at $4,321.20.

"The unrelenting surge in Treasury yields has set gold on course for its 4th weekly decline over the past five weeks," said Han Tan, chief market analyst at Bybit.

The US benchmark 10-year bond yield hit a fresh 19-year high, increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.

"The zero-yielding precious metal has struggled against a cacophony of headwinds, including persistent upside inflation risks, runaway Treasury yields, and a hawkish Fed," Tan added.

Since the onset of the US-Israeli war on Iran, rising energy prices kept inflation concerns alive, forcing central banks to adopt tighter policy frameworks to keep price pressures under check.

The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter-point last week, its first increase in three years, and signalled more hikes ahead. Traders are pricing in a 66% chance of an October hike and a 93% chance of one in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.

Gold is traditionally considered an inflation hedge and a safe investment during geopolitical uncertainty. However, higher interest rates tarnish its attractiveness as investors turn to yield-bearing assets. Bullion has fallen about 19% from its February 27 session high.

Negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, according to sources. Oil prices dropped about 3% as some supply fears eased.

Spot silver gained 0.5% to $64.26 per ounce, platinum rose 1.7% to $1,780.28, and palladium fell 0.3% to $1,270.30. All three metals were poised for weekly losses.

data.title: Wall Street climbs as investors buy AI stocks; Microsoft rallies
data.description:
Key points:
  • Akamai Technologies surges on $11.6 billion Anthropic deal
  • Microsoft revamps Copilot with code generation, agentic AI tools
  • S&P 500 +0.45%, Nasdaq +0.50%, Dow +0.78%

By Noel Randewich and Johann M Cherian

Wall Street climbed on Friday, lifted by Microsoft and other AI-related technology stocks, while high oil prices and a recent surge in US Treasury yields kept investors on edge.

Gains in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq capped a volatile week driven by uncertainty about what industries will win and lose from artificial intelligence, and by concerns about the US war with Iran and a surge in US Treasury yields.

Microsoft rallied 3.3%, lifting its 2026 gain to 7%, after the software giant unveiled several new capabilities in its Copilot app, including a coding tool and an always-on AI agent.

Akamai Technologies surged 6% after an $11.6 billion cloud services deal with AI leader Anthropic. The deal includes a warrant that could give Anthropic up to 5% of Akamai.

"That's a positive from the standpoint that people are still investing, deals are still being done," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments in Atlanta. "It's another circular deal, so OK ... but Akamai stock is up."

Chip maker Qualcomm gained 5.4% and Dell advanced 6.6%.

Meta Platforms dipped 3.6%. The social media company's stock has soared about 13% this week amid a strong reception to its Muse AI agent, which analysts say could benefit tech infrastructure stocks, while challenging banks, online shopping platforms and other consumer businesses.

The S&P 500 was up 0.45% at 7,738.67 points.

The Nasdaq gained 0.50% to 27,073.90 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.78% at 51,747.99 points.

Seven of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by information technology , up 1.06%, followed by a 0.85% gain in industrials .

The S&P 500 was on track to gain over 1% for the week, while the Nasdaq was heading for a weekly gain of about 2% after it notched a record-high close on Tuesday.

The S&P 500 this week has traded just under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023, according to LSEG data. AI-related heavyweights are responsible for much of the recent increase in earnings expectations.

A report that US and Iranian negotiators continued to explore a phased path out of the war, which would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade, helped market sentiment.

Data also showed strong AI-related capital expenditures boosted demand for key manufactured capital goods, outpacing expectations in August.

Brent crude eased but remained above $100 a barrel. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note hit a fresh 19-year high and was last up 3.4 basis points at 5.196%.

Traders see a 66% chance of the Federal Reserve increasing interest rates by at least 25 basis points in October, up from around 50% earlier this week, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed.

US President Donald Trump said he had a "very productive meeting" with President Xi Jinping, following a three-day summit that showcased personal diplomacy rather than big breakthroughs in economic relations.

Magazine publisher People Inc jumped 11% after a report said MGM Resorts International was discussing a bid for the company.

Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.7-to-one ratio.

The S&P 500 posted three new highs and 31 new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 44 new highs and 147 new lows.

data.title: Erste Group to launch a voluntary tender offer to increase its shareholding in Erste Bank Polska
data.description:
Erste Group Bank AG

by Thomas Sommerauer/ Simone Pilz

Public disclosure of inside information according to article 17 MAR

Erste Group Bank AG: Erste Group to launch a voluntary tender offer to increase its shareholding in Erste Bank Polska

Building on transformational acquisition of a 49% controlling stake in January 2026

Vienna (pta000/25.09.2026/20:05 UTC+2)

Erste Group Bank AG ("Erste Group") announces its intention to launch a voluntary tender offer (the "Offer"), for 100% cash consideration, for shares in Erste Bank Polska S.A. ("Erste Bank Polska" or "EBP") to increase its current 49% shareholding by up to an additional 26% stake and to deepen its exposure to one of its core CEE markets. The Offer price will be approx. PLN 713 per share.

Offer structure and intended ownership range. Erste Group intends to acquire between c. 1% and 26% of EBP's share capital, with the objective of increasing Erste Group's stake to above 50% but not exceeding 75%. This is in line with the investor commitment Erste Group made to the Polish Financial Supervision Authority ("PFSA") in connection with its acquisition of a 49% stake in EBP in January 2026, under which it undertook to maintain a free float of at least 25% of EBP's shares. The Offer will be conditional upon fulfilment (or, waiver of the first and/or second) of: (1) a minimum acceptance condition – the shares tendered, together with Erste Group's existing 49% holding, representing at least 50% of EBP's share capital and total voting rights; (2) a free float condition – shareholders representing at least 25% of EBP's shares entering into a commitment with EBP and Erste Group not to tender their shares; and, (3) a regulatory approval condition – the Offer will be conditional upon regulatory approval from the PFSA for Erste Group to cross the 50% voting threshold at EBP (unless such approval is obtained prior to the formal announcement of the Offer, in which case the Offer will not be made subject to this condition). If the free-float condition is not met, but Offer acceptances remain below 26% of EBP's shares, Erste Group may elect to waive the condition. Should more than 26% of EBP's shareholders tender their shares – and the free float condition therefore not be satisfied – Erste Group intends to declare the Offer unsuccessful and remain a 49% shareholder in EBP. The detailed terms and conditions of the Offer will be set out in the tender offer circular in accordance with applicable rules.

Details on the Offer price. The Offer price will correspond to the 3-month-volume weighted average price (VWAP) per share preceding 28 September 2026, which is the expected date of filing the notification of the intention to announce the Offer with the PFSA. Based on preliminary data available as of the date of this disclosure this is expected to correspond to approx. PLN 713 per share. It reflects a 22.1% premium over the PLN 584 per share reference price[1] of Erste Group's May 2025 announcement of the acquisition of the 49% stake – a price that embedded a premium for a strategic and controlling stake. It also sits at the upper end of EBP's 52-week trading range.

Key next milestones. Erste Group has already initiated the regulatory approval process with the PFSA to exceed 50% ownership in Erste Bank Polska. Erste Group expects to launch the Offer at the start of November 2026, with a subscription period of 30 days (extendable in accordance with applicable rules). Completion and settlement are anticipated in December 2026.

Full internal funding, sound strategic and financial rationale. Erste Group intends to fund the Offer exclusively from internal resources and targets a post-offer CET1 ratio of >14.25%. Increasing Erste Group's stake in EBP extends its exposure to Poland, one of the fastest-growing economies and among the most profitable banking markets in Europe. The proposed increase of shareholding in EBP to up to 75% would further strengthen Poland's contribution to consolidated net income and is expected to be EPS accretive from 2027.

[1] The purchase price of PLN 584 per share for the acquisition of 49% of Santander Bank Polska was based on the exchange rate agreed between the parties in the share purchase agreement. At exchange rates as of the days of payment of instalments of the purchase price, the purchase price per share corresponds to PLN 577.5.

Erste Group shares (ISIN AT0000652011) are listed on the Vienna, Prague and Bucharest stock exchanges and traded on various electronic marketplaces. The bonds issued by Erste Group Bank AG are admitted to trading on the following regulated markets: Vienna, Luxembourg, Budapest, Bucharest, Stuttgart. The five biggest listed bonds of Erste Group Bank AG in terms of issue volume have the following ISINs: AT0000A324F5, AT0000A33MP9, AT0000A39GD4, AT0000A3B0X2, XS1750974658.

data.title: Meta's Muse Read-Through for Cable, Telecoms Not as Bad as Feared — Market Talk
data.description: The sour market sentiment toward cable and telecommunications stocks following the release of Meta's Muse AI agent is likely overblown, Morgan Stanley analysts write in a note, writing that investors have "not been discerning enough in assessing the risks posed by the rise of agents." Yes, the ease with which consumers can use AI agents to manage their bills and subscriptions is notable, but the pricing pressure on cable and telecom names may be less than the market is expecting. "Agents should lower search and switching costs, improve consumers' ability to identify better offers and potentially increase pressure on acquisition costs, retention spending and ARPU," the analysts write. "But the magnitude and source of that pressure could vary considerably by provider and product." They see cable names as more exposed than wireless stocks. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

data.title: Comcast Stock Hits Its Lowest Level in More Than a Decade. Why the Trouble Runs Deep. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mariapaula Gonzalez

Comcast has faced serious headwinds and the trouble extends far beyond a competitive broadband market.

Shares of Comcast fell 2.1% to $21.67 Friday after KeyBanc analysts downgraded the stock to Underweight, the equivalent of a Sell rating, from Sector Weight with a $18 price target. Analyst Brandon Nispel said Friday that Comcast has lost subscribers faster than expected, theme parks have slowed down, and the planned move to separate from NBCUniversal won't boost the stock.

The stock was on pace to close at its lowest level since Oct. 11, 2013, when shares hit $21.57.

The average analyst rating on Comcast is a Hold, according to the 29 analysts polled by FactSet.

Nispel noted that broadband and mobile operators have been facing intense competition from rivals offering cheap, high-speed internet for as little as $30 to $40 a month. As a result, he projects that Comcast will lose 558,000 broadband customers in 2026 and 665,000 in 2027. The analyst added that Comcast's view that competitors' prices are irrational but refusal to match them traps the company in a lose-lose situation.

While Wall Street expects a solid earnings rebound for Comcast's core connectivity and platforms operations-home to its flagship Xfinity broadband, mobile, and pay-TV services-Nispel remains skeptical. Beyond ongoing subscriber losses, he said the company's heavy investments and massive upfront restructuring costs could weigh heavily on fiscal fourth-quarter earnings.

Performance at Comcast's Universal theme parks has dwindled, and Nispel expects growth to remain muted. Comcast attributed recent struggles to softer attendance, which has fallen sharply since June. Even hype around the new Epic Universe park in Orland hasn't prevented a deceleration in visitors. Though Wall Street expects a 9% rebound in theme parks in 2027, Nispel projects growth to remain flat.

Nispel is cautious about the NBCUniversal spinoff, noting that Comcast might buy back stock and lose a key support mechanism for the share price. Still, he thinks the separation could pave the way for an eventual merger with rival Charter Communications. Joining forces would reduce back-office costs and reach more than 130 million homes, giving both companies massive scale against telecommunications rivals.

Rival Charter Communications stock declined 2.7%.

Write to Mariapaula Gonzalez at mariapaula.gonzalez@barrons.com

data.title: Converse pauses social media ads, marketing after racism uproar, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
Nike-owned sneaker brand Converse told employees it is pausing all marketing this week after an earlier advertisement sparked outrage for evoking imagery of the Ku Klux Klan and lynching, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing a person familiar with the decision.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Nike did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Converse pulled the advertisement after facing public backlash last week and apologized, saying "we got this wrong."

The ad showed the lower half of ​a person wearing a white, calf-length skirt-like garment, ⁠which critics said resembled a KKK robe. The person ​was featured holding black sneakers.

The images were part of a campaign for Converse's Chuck 70 X sneaker, created in collaboration with Karina, a member of the K-pop group Aespa.

The ad also drew scrutiny from US lawmakers. In a statement on Monday, the Congressional Black Caucus said it was "deeply disturbed and disappointed by Converse’s decision to release this advertising campaign," and that it would request a meeting with Nike executives.

Converse sales have dropped for 13 consecutive quarters, most recently tumbling 34% on a constant-currency basis in the fourth quarter.

Nike, which is set to report first-quarter earnings next week, is still facing significant obstacles as CEO Elliott Hill tries to turn around the business. Shares have fallen more than 40% this year as investors seek clear signs that Hill's nearly two-year effort to revive growth is gaining ‌traction.

data.title: Evonik gains after report of BASF takeover approach (update)
data.description:
Update 9:35a.m.: Adds Evonik comment.

Evonik rose 10% in German trading after a report that BASF () () approached its German chemical rival about a takeover. BASF fell 2.3%.

BASF recently made a proposal to Evonik (EKVIY) and its largest holders, the RAG-Stiftung foundation, according to a Financial Times report  on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Evonik confirmed in a statement on Friday that it received a non-binding approach from BASF on a takeover offer for all Evonik's shares. No talks are currently taking place. Evonik declined to comment beyond its legal obligations.

BASF has been talking to advisers about a potential offer for Evonik since earlier this year and is continuing to work a possible deal, according to the FT report. The position of RAG-Stiftung, which has a 44% stake in Evonik, will be key to whether any transaction can happen.

BASF and AG-Stiftung declined to comment to the FT.

Reuters, citing a person familiar with the matter, reported on Friday that Evonik is not aware of a takeover approach from BASF.

The FT item comes after Dealreporter on Monday first reported that BASF explored a potential deal with Evonik this year. One source downplayed the possibility of a deal as BASF is “cash constrained” and will get the Agricultural Solutions IPO completed before it does an acquisition.

data.title: Nigeria's Amni, TotalEnergies approve $800 million offshore gas project
data.description:
By Tife Owolabi

Nigeria's state oil firm NNPC Ltd said on Friday that a proposed $800 million offshore natural gas project by local producer Amni International and TotalEnergies had reached a final investment decision, marking one of the biggest recent investments in Nigeria's upstream gas sector.

  • The Ima gas project located on Oil Mining Leases 112 and 117 is expected to produce around 300 million standard cubic feet of gas per day at peak output.

  • Gas from the project will feed Nigeria LNG's Train 7 expansion, boosting the Bonny Island plant's production capacity to 30 million tonnes per year from 22 million.

  • NNPC said the investment was enabled by President Bola Tinubu's oil reforms, which introduced fiscal incentives for gas projects, streamlined contracting processes and lowered development costs.

  • According to NNPC, which grants approvals for such projects, the Ima project is the fourth major gas development to reach FID since Tinubu's 2024 oil reforms.

data.title: Ligand Pharma a new Outperform at Barclays on biopharma royalty aggregation
data.description:
Key points:
  • Barclays initiated Ligand Pharmaceuticals with an Outperform rating, saying that the company's transition to loyalty aggregation has the potential to generate long-term revenue growth of greater than 20%.
  • The investment bank has a price target of $345 (~15% upside based on Sept. 24 close). 
  • Analyst Glan Santangelo said that despite Ligand's strong performance year-to-date—up ~59%—"core fundamentals and outlook remain somewhat underappreciated especially given the expanded deal team + ample cash generation, which increases the company's ability to source and execute deals."

data.title: A 10% risk-free yield? For some, yes.
data.description:
By Brett Arends

This could be a bargain, especially for very high earners and those in high-tax locations

Muni bonds are on sale and can shelter income in high-tax locations like New York City, where high earners pay federal, state and city taxes

Low-risk municipal bonds are now yielding as high as 5% tax-free, thanks to the recent turmoil in the bond market.

Those could be a bargain, especially for very high earners and those in high-tax locations like New York City and California. But advisers warn these bargains aren't always as simple as they might seem. As usual, you need to do the math.

"I love municipal bonds, and they're 'on sale,' which is a rarity," says Michael McMeans, a financial planner with Silverling Financial in Columbus, Ohio. "Anyone making over $400,000 should be looking at them - and for the most part, they're not. Huge value."

Joon Um, a financial planner with Secure Tax & Accounting in Beverly Hills, Calif., says: "For high earners in places like New York City, munis can look very attractive right now. ... A 5% to 6% tax-free yield could potentially equal 10%-plus on a taxable-equivalent basis."

But, he adds: "I wouldn't chase the tax benefit alone. Credit quality, duration and liquidity still matter. For high-net-worth clients, I think munis can make a lot of sense when they fit the overall tax and investment strategy."

A "taxable-equivalent yield" is what you'd have to earn from a taxable bond, such as Treasury bonds or corporate debt, to end up with the same income after tax. Income from municipal bonds is typically exempt from federal income taxes, as well as the state and local taxes of the issuing municipality.

"It is a case-by-case and state-by-state calculation to determine whether munis are in the client's best interest," says Donald LaGrange, a financial adviser at Murphy & Sylvest in Dallas. He recently found that a prospective client in New York City could save $37,000 in total taxes on their bonds by switching to municipals. "Combined taxes were taking about 47% of her interest," he notes.

Very high earners can pay more than 50 cents on the dollar in total taxes on their top dollars of investment income. That includes 37% federal income tax, plus a 3.8% federal surtax on investment income, plus state and local taxes rising as high as 13.3% in California and 14.8% in New York City.

If you're paying 50% tax, you'd have to earn 10% on a taxable bond to end up keeping 5% after taxes.

The biggest tax benefit from municipals accrues to those with the highest incomes in the highest-tax locations - but you don't need to be a multimillionaire to benefit. A middle-class single filer in New York City, for example, could be paying a top marginal tax rate of 32% across city, state and federal taxes. For them, a 5% tax-free municipal is the equivalent of a taxable bond paying 7.4%.

That's better than investment-grade corporate bonds. The Vanguard Long-Term Corporate Bond ETF VCLT has an annual yield of 6.2%, and the iShares 10+ Year Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF IGLB yields 6.4% (using a standardized measure from the Securities and Exchange Commission that extrapolates from the coupons of the last 30 days).

But there are several caveats with municipal bonds that investors need to understand.

To get these higher yields, you must take on some risk. That's true even if you stick to "general obligation" municipal bonds, which are backed by the full faith and credit of the state or municipality, and which usually have the lowest risk of default. To get 5% yields, you need to buy longer-term municipals - often those that don't mature for 25 or 30 years.

But those involve interest-rate and inflation risks. In practice, this means that over short periods those bonds can be very volatile in price (as we are seeing now), especially when the Federal Reserve raises short-term rates.

"Be sure you understand the volatility associated with longer-duration bonds before investing," says financial planner Edward Mahaffy of ClientFirst Wealth, Legacy & Estate Planning in Fort Worth, Texas. "Long-duration bonds tend to pay the highest yields and can be enticing, but they come with greater interest-rate risk."

It also means that over long terms, particularly the full life of the bond, you are taking on inflation risk.

If inflation averages 2% a year over the next 30 years, consumer prices will rise 81%. If it averages 3%, they'll rise 142%. This will make an enormous difference to the actual purchasing-power returns of anyone buying a 30-year bond with fixed 5% interest rates.

Kevin Brady of Wealthspire Advisors in New York City says he's mostly sticking to shorter- and intermediate-length munis. "We target a duration between four to five years," he says. "You can get yields in or close to the 4% range at that duration, which on a tax-equivalent basis would be about 8% or so."

But financial planner Matthew Chancey, founder of Tax Alpha Companies in Tampa, Fla., is a skeptic. "Here's the trick behind 'taxable-equivalent yield': The bond really pays you about 5%. The other 5% is make-believe," he says. "It's the tax you didn't have to pay, dressed up to look like money you earned."

He thinks high-net-worth individuals may be better off looking at investing in areas such as in real estate, where the federal tax code offers generous tax breaks. "In that world, nobody asks, 'How do I earn less so I'm taxed less?'" he notes. "They ask, 'How do I keep all the income, and change what the taxman calls it?' The tax code actually lets you do that."

You need to be wealthy to take advantage, he adds, but most of those paying 50% marginal tax rates already qualify.

Many advisers point out that the tax break on muni bonds needs to be viewed in the broader context of your overall financial picture and your plans. Taxes are only one factor.

And there are a few extra caveats. One is that some municipal bonds may trigger the alternative minimum tax at the federal level. The other is that municipals only make sense in taxable investment accounts. You may be able to improve your after-tax returns by contributing more to tax-sheltered accounts, such as your 401(k) or IRA, and investing in taxable bonds or stocks.

Right now, 30-year Treasury bonds BX:TMUBMUSD30Y are paying 5.5%, and the income is taxable at the federal, state and city levels. Meanwhile, many long-term munis are paying 5%. So mathematically, the munis will produce better returns after tax, unless the marginal tax rate on top incomes falls to 9% or below.

Here's a simple call: That's not going to happen.

-Brett Arends

data.title: Perplexity AI sued by startup for allegedly stealing 'wake word' technology
data.description:
By Blake Brittain

Startup DaVoice has sued Perplexity AI in California federal court for allegedly stealing trade secrets related to "wake word" technology for AI assistants.

  • The heavily redacted complaint filed on Thursday said that Perplexity stole DaVoice's secrets after the companies collaborated on unspecified technology "built with DaVoice’s proprietary source code, inference logic, network architecture, training approaches, training data, and know-how"

  • A Perplexity spokesperson on Friday called the lawsuit "a baseless attempt to claim ownership of standard wake-word technology" and said the companies' agreement "expressly protects our right to develop our own 'similar, equal or competitive products or services.'"

  • Spokespeople and attorneys for DaVoice did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit.

  • DaVoice specializes in technology that allows devices to continuously listen for "wake words" to activate them

  • The startup said that it has collaborated with companies including Volkswagen and internet-of-things company Samsara

  • Perplexity is best known for its AI-powered search engine technology and Comet browser and AI assistant

The case is DaVoice v. Perplexity AI Inc, US District Court for the Northern District of California, No. 3:26-cv-10909.

For DaVoice: Davida Brook and Ian Crosby of Susman Godfrey

For Perplexity: attorney information not yet available

data.title: Cruise Bookings Are Strong — Market Talk
data.description: UBS analysts say they recently caught up with one of the largest U.S. cruise sellers, who noted clear skies, both figuratively and literally. The seller noted that August and September have marked a record in terms of inactivity during hurricane season, and as a result, booking volumes have been strong, the analysts say in a research note. data.title: HSBC Upgrades Synopsys, Sets Street-High $700 Target
data.description:
Synopsys , the chip design software company, rose 1.81% intraday, as of 10:20 a.m. ET, after HSBC upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to a Street-high $700 from $490. The target implies over 60% upside from current levels.

HSBC set the target at 35x its fiscal 2027 earnings-per-share estimate of $20.01, rolling its valuation forward from 33x fiscal 2026. That estimate sits 13% above consensus and is the highest on Wall Street, according to the firm.

Synopsys is moving its business model toward royalties, which HSBC expects to drive earnings growth, and the bank sees agentic AI lifting demand for electronic design automation tools. The call follows a strong fiscal third quarter, in which Synopsys earned $3.91 a share on a non-GAAP basis on revenue of $2.48 billion, beating estimates of $3.67 and $2.44 billion, and raised its full-year outlook.

data.title: Amazon Stocks Move Lower as Anthropic Commits $11.6 Billion Elsewhere
data.description:
Amazon , the cloud and e-commerce giant, faced a fresh reminder that backing an AI heavyweight does not secure every dollar of its computing budget. Shares stood at $248.515 at 10.22am ET time on September 25 as investors weighed Anthropic's seven-year, $11.6 billion commitment to cloud infrastructure provider Akamai. The valuation snapshot puts Amazon just 0.33% below its $249.35 GF Value estimateessentially fair value, with little valuation cushion.

The deal covers CPU workloads, and Akamai estimates roughly $5.5 billion in related capital spending. According to Reuters' reporting, the arrangement also includes a warrant potentially giving Anthropic a 5% stake in Akamai. An additional $9 billion of business could expand the relationship further. That gives Anthropic another substantial source of computing capacity, although the announcement does not establish that existing workloads are moving away from Amazon Web Services.

For Amazon shareholders, the investment payoff and the cloud payoff deserve separate scrutiny. Amazon's second-quarter earnings release reported $53.4 billion in non-operating pretax other income, primarily from its Anthropic investments. Those gains can lift reported earnings without representing AWS sales. Amazon can benefit from Anthropic's rising value while another supplier wins its next infrastructure contract. The question is how much of that expanding computing budget AWS captures.

data.title: KeyBanc Revamps Comcast Stock Price Target for Rest of 2026
data.description:
Comcast is facing a tougher setup into the end of 2026, according to KeyBanc Capital Markets, which downgraded the stock to Underweight and cut its price target to $18 as broadband subscriber losses deepen and pressure builds across cable profitability and theme parks.

Analyst Brandon Nispel's new target implies roughly 19% downside from Comcast's latest close.

The biggest concern is broadband.

KeyBanc expects Comcast's domestic broadband net losses to widen to 665,000 in 2027, significantly worse than the consensus estimate for a 482,000 decline.

Competitive pricing is at the center of the problem.

Rivals are offering 1-gigabit internet plans for roughly $30 to $40 per month, leaving Comcast with an uncomfortable choice: avoid matching those promotions and risk losing more customers, or respond with lower pricing and pressure average revenue per user.

That makes the broadband challenge both a subscriber and profitability problem.

Cable and connectivity EBITDA may also struggle to recover as quickly as investors expect. Comcast has described 2026 as a year of investment while undertaking what it has called the largest cost transformation in the company history.

Theme parks add another pressure point.

Universal attendance weakened through August, with total attendance down 3% year over year. Epic Universe's average daily attendance fell to roughly 13,000 from 16,000 in July.

Nispel also sees limited upside from Comcast's planned NBCUniversal spin-off, arguing deteriorating fundamentals and reduced share-repurchase support could offset the potential benefits.

Investor takeaway

For Comcast investors, the downgrade suggests the stock's low valuation may not be enough to overcome weakening fundamentals.

Comcast trades at roughly 5 times estimated 2027 adjusted EBITDA versus a three-year average near 6 times, but KeyBanc sees further downside because earnings pressure is spreading across multiple businesses.

Investors should watch broadband churn, ARPU, cable EBITDA, park attendance and the economics of the NBCUniversal separation.

The key issue is whether Comcast can stabilize broadband without sacrificing pricing.

Until that becomes clearer, KeyBanc believes the turnaround risk outweighs the apparent valuation discount.

data.title: Microsoft Revamps Copilot as AI Spending Scrutiny Grows
data.description:
Microsoft (MSFT) is overhauling Copilot with a stronger focus on enterprise customers, rolling out a unified assistant that combines consumer and workplace capabilities while giving companies more control over how employees use and pay for artificial intelligence.

The redesign has been in development for roughly six months and begins rolling out through Microsoft's Frontier program.

The new Copilot app is organized around several major features.

Home brings together Chat and Cowork, while Code lets users build and run software using GitHub Copilot technology. Autopilot, previously called Scout, functions as a persistent agent designed to act proactively for users.

But the most important addition for large companies may be FinOps for AI.

Microsoft says the tool is designed to help organizations track AI usage, control spending and connect that spending to business value.

FinOps for AI is a shared discipline for managing AI spend and optimizing it for business value, said Jared Spataro, chief marketing officer for Microsoft AI at Work.

Administrators will be able to manage spending policies at scale, route requests for additional AI credits through existing approval systems, and decide which model families different employee groups can access.

That matters as enterprise AI adoption becomes more expensive and complex.

Microsoft is effectively trying to make Copilot not just the interface employees use for AI, but also the management layer companies use to govern it.

The timing is notable. Meta is gaining attention with its Muse personal AI agent, while Qualcomm has introduced platforms designed to support personal agents across devices.

Investor takeaway

For Microsoft investors, the Copilot overhaul shifts the monetization discussion toward enterprise control and recurring usage.

The key question is whether companies see enough productivity gains to increase AI spending rather than limit it.

Investors should watch Copilot adoption, paid seat growth, agent usage, Azure consumption and whether FinOps tools reduce enterprise resistance to rising AI costs.

The biggest opportunity is that Microsoft already owns much of the software stack enterprises use every day.

If Copilot becomes the layer companies use to deploy, monitor and budget AI agents, Microsoft could capture more value from AI spending without relying solely on model access itself.

Microsoft plans to unveil additional Copilot features at Ignite from November 17 through November 20.

data.title: American Drivers Are Turning Away From Ford and GM
data.description:
General Motors and Ford Motor are on track to post the steepest U.S. market-share declines among major automakers in 2026, according to Cox Automotive, as high gas prices push more consumers toward fuel-efficient vehicles and Asian brands continue gaining ground.

Ford's U.S. vehicle sales are expected to fall 8.8% through the first three quarters of the year.

That would cut Ford's market share by nearly a full percentage point to 12.5%.

GM is also underperforming the broader industry. Cox expects its U.S. market share to fall to 16.7% from 17.4% a year earlier.

The broader U.S. auto market is projected to decline 6.2% year to date through September 30.

Those declines would leave Ford and GM with the two largest market-share losses among the 13 automakers tracked by Cox.

The bigger structural shift is happening across Detroit.

Cox expects the combined share of GM, Ford and Stellantis to fall to an all-time low of roughly 36%, even as Stellantis itself gains share.

Asian brands are expected to account for more than half of U.S. new-vehicle sales for a second consecutive quarter, approaching record-high market share levels, Cox senior economist Charlie Chesbrough said.

Toyota is expected to post year-over-year growth in the third quarter and continues narrowing the gap with GM despite supply constraints on key models.

Hyundai Motor Group is also expected to deliver another strong quarter, with sales rising from both a year earlier and the prior quarter and coming in ahead of Ford.

Tesla is struggling as well. Cox projects its year-to-date U.S. sales will fall 18.9%, reducing market share to 3.0% from 3.7%.

Investor takeaway

For Ford and GM investors, the immediate issue is not just falling industry sales but relative share loss.

If high gas prices continue pushing buyers toward more efficient vehicles, product mix becomes increasingly important.

Investors should watch market share, incentives, truck and SUV demand, hybrid penetration and whether Detroit automakers can stabilize sales without sacrificing margins.

The key risk is that Asian manufacturers continue gaining share while Ford and GM remain concentrated in less fuel-efficient categories.

A recovery in gasoline prices or stronger hybrid offerings could help, but Cox's forecast shows the competitive gap is widening for now.

data.title: Private-Equity Linked Insurers Drive Affiliated Investments, Regulatory Group Finds — WSJ
data.description:
By Heather Gillers

Life insurers hold $321 billion in affiliated investments and about half of them belong to 10 insurers that have relationships with private-equity companies, according to a report Thursday from the National Association of Insurance Commissioners.

The group, which is made up of the top insurance regulator in every state, classifies investments as affiliated if they are backed by or sold by companies related to the insurer even if the related company is not the one on the hook for payments. Such holdings have grown as private asset managers have bought up insurers and sold them private credit and other alternative investments to put in their portfolios.

Affiliated investments tumbled into the spotlight this summer after two insurers controlled by Dodgers owner Mark Walter revealed that they had discovered, after receiving federal subpoenas, that they had failed to properly disclose a combined $20 billion in such holdings.

Insurers with some of the highest concentrations of affiliated investments include Security Benefit, Athene and Commonwealth, The Wall Street Journal has found. The NAIC found most life insurers have very limited affiliated investments. Industrywide, the share is about 5%.

In its report, the NAIC found the highest dollar amount of affiliated holdings-$188 billion-fell into the category of "other long-term investments" and the second-highest-$76 billion-was in asset backed securities. The 10 private-equity linked life insurers accounted for 95% of the affiliated asset-backed securities, the report said.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
